findings.title: Flex conversion of .small-action breaks right-aligned action button
findings.body: Converting .small-action to a flex container invalidates the existing right-alignment mechanism: floats are ignored on flex items, so the button rule still using float: right no longer pushes the action to the right edge. At the same time .small-action-desc is not given flex: 1, so it shrink-wraps instead of consuming the row width. The result is that the button sits immediately after the description rather than at the far right, regressing the small-action row layout. Give .small-action-desc flex: 1 and/or give the button margin-left: auto.

findings.title: order mixin uses 0-based values for 1-based legacy flexbox property
findings.body: The legacy flexbox properties -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group use a 1-based initial value, while the standard order property uses 0. Emitting the same $val for both means the mixin does not provide equivalent behavior: for example @include order(1) has no effect in browsers using the legacy box syntax, and other values are shifted by one relative to modern flexbox. Since this mixin is intended to abstract ordering for the header layout, emit $val + 1 for the box-ordinal-group properties.
